messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — customer ACME reported their March invoice looks ~40% lower than expected, they claim requests were throttled but still billable. can we confirm meter?
Maria Gomez: Which metric — tokens or embeds?
Alex Chen: Tokens. they sent examples of chat sessions. says service returned 429 but client retried. suspect dedupe logic in ingestion dropped retries so undercounted.
Ben Patel: I pulled the raw edge logs for their org_id and see a flurry of 429s between 2026-03-12 14:03–14:10 UTC, then a lot of retries with identical request_ids. Our ingest pipeline currently dedups by request_id within 30s window.
Sophie Li: @Ben can you paste sample log lines?
Ben Patel: Sure — sample: ```json
{"ts":"2026-03-12T14:03:21Z","org":"acme","req_id":"r_9f3a","status":429,"tokens":120}
{"ts":"2026-03-12T14:03:23Z","org":"acme","req_id":"r_9f3a-retry-1","status":200,"tokens":120}```
Ben Patel: Our dedupe sees r_9f3a and r_9f3a-retry-1 as same bundle (we canonicalize IDs) — that made the retry non-billable because we mark deduped ones as cache hits. That explains undercount.
Maria Gomez: Oof. So billed tokens were lower because we treated retries as duplicates and set billable=false. Is this customer-facing policy documented?
Jordan Park: Not really, this was an optimization to prevent double-billing during network retries. But we didn't account for clients that change request_id suffixes.
Alex Chen: ACME is pushing for a credit for March and wants the corrected numbers before their finance close. They asked for a CSV of events and an estimated credit amount.
Sophie Li: Can we compute the delta quickly? Ben — estimate how many additional billable tokens in that window if we treat retries as separate billable requests.
Ben Patel: Quick query on billing mirror (approx): ```sql
SELECT sum(tokens) as tokens_if_billed
FROM billing_events
WHERE org='acme' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-12' AND '2026-03-13' AND request_id like 'r_9f3a%';
-- result: 1,280,000 tokens
-- currently billed: 768,000 tokens
-- delta: 512,000 tokens```
Ben Patel: Delta ~= 512k tokens. At their plan price that’s $51.20. Need confirm exact SKU mapping and rounding.
Maria Gomez: Small amount but customer expects formal correction. Requesting approval to issue one-off credit and run backfill to update metering ledger.
Alex Chen: @Jordan can you draft the customer note and approval request for finance lead? Also include audit log showing dedupe rule and sample events.
Jordan Park: Drafted note: "We discovered a deduplication edge case that caused some retry requests to be treated as non-billable. We will apply a one-time credit of $51.20 and run a metering backfill; attached CSV of events and SQL used." Need approval from Finance Lead (cc:@Maria).
Maria Gomez: Approve the credit and backfill, please proceed. :white_check_mark:
billing-bot: Automated check — backfill job prerequisites: export snapshot, dry-run, approval present.
Sophie Li: Next steps for eng: Ben to create a dry-run backfill that writes to a temp ledger and produces CSV. Ben — ETA?
Ben Patel: Will start dry-run today, expect results by EOD. I'll include per-request diffs and a checksum.
Alex Chen: Also let's add a small ops note to docs: dedupe canonicalization can collapse retry suffixes — we'll either stop canonicalizing or tag retried requests as billable when status=200 after 429.
Jordan Park: I'll send customer note after dry-run confirms numbers. Thanks team.
Maria Gomez: Add a quick postmortem to finance/incidents later so we have an audit trail.
Alex Chen: Thanks all.
